origins.section: 9.1. Several Codes Approve, and a Partial Approval Covers Only Part of the Amount
9.2. A Decline Is Final for Its Request, and Its Code Says Who Could Change the Answer
9.3. An Error Code Reports a Failure, Not a Decision About the Card
9.4. Later Editions Put the Category in the First Digit

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-taxi-fare: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-taxi-fare: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-taxi-fare: 9.1's table gives 10 as approved for a partial amount with the action 'collect the rest some other way', so collecting the other 12.00 is decided.
recorded.prompt:q-atm-pin: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-atm-pin: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-atm-pin: 9.2 says the issuer counts each wrong PIN it checks, so the resend is one more failed try toward the limit and 75.
recorded.prompt:q-monday-release: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-monday-release: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-monday-release: 9.3 says 30 is a format error in the sender's message that fails again until a developer fixes it, and gives this case: after a release every purchase comes back 30.
recorded.prompt:q-reversal-4000: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-reversal-4000: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-reversal-4000: 9.4 says 4000 accepts a reversal and a sender treating every code outside 0 as a failure keeps resending a reversal the receiver applied, then parks it.

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-taxi-fare:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-taxi-fare:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-taxi-fare:a: 9.1: read as a full approval, the merchant hands over the goods and is paid only the approved part (partly true: 10 is an approval code).
recorded.prompt:q-taxi-fare:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-taxi-fare:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-taxi-fare:b: 9.1 lists 10 as an approval and says that read as a decline the issuer holds money no sale will use.
recorded.prompt:q-taxi-fare:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-taxi-fare:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-taxi-fare:d: 9.1: asking the issuer again for the full amount doesn't help, the card has nothing more to give.
recorded.prompt:q-atm-pin:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-atm-pin:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-atm-pin:b: 9.2 places 55 among the declines only the cardholder can change with the right PIN, not a passing fault like 9.3's 91 or 96.
recorded.prompt:q-atm-pin:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-atm-pin:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-atm-pin:c: 9.2 says the issuer counts each wrong PIN it checks, so the resend is checked, not repeated unchecked (partly true: the same request gets the same decision).
recorded.prompt:q-atm-pin:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-atm-pin:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-atm-pin:d: 9.2 says the issuer counts each wrong PIN it checks, with nothing tying the count to a cardholder typing at the keypad.
recorded.prompt:q-monday-release:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-monday-release:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-monday-release:b: 9.3 says an error code reports a failure, not a decision about the card, and every purchase comes back 30, so other cards fail too.
recorded.prompt:q-monday-release:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-monday-release:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-monday-release:c: 9.3 says a 30 request sent again unchanged fails again.
recorded.prompt:q-monday-release:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-monday-release:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-monday-release:d: 9.3 puts the fix with the sender's developer, not the receiver (implied rather than stated outright).
recorded.prompt:q-reversal-4000:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-reversal-4000:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-reversal-4000:b: 9.4's listing shows 4000 as REVERSAL_ACCEPTED, contradicting 'no original to undo' (partly true: its outcome matches the key, only the reason is wrong).
recorded.prompt:q-reversal-4000:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-reversal-4000:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-reversal-4000:c: 9.4 says this sender keeps resending, so a reversal never leaves the queue at the first answer (partly true: 4 is the reversal category).
recorded.prompt:q-reversal-4000:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-reversal-4000:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-reversal-4000:d: 9.4's sender reads the first digit and keeps resending; nothing makes it read 4000 as 00 (partly grounded in 'in 1987 the same acknowledgements are 00').

gates.says: each of the 4 questions keys exactly 1 of its distinct options and every option carries the sentence its reader is shown
each of the 4 questions cites a passage the ledger still digests to the value this exercise was built from
